definitions.explanation: A cherry variety whose blossoms have many overlapping petals, blooming a little later than ordinary single-petaled cherries. Fuller and heavier-looking than {染井吉野|そめいよしの}.

examples.japanese: {八重桜|やえざくら}が{満開|まんかい}だ。
examples.english: The double cherry blossoms are in full bloom.

examples.japanese: ソメイヨシノより{八重桜|やえざくら}の{方|ほう}が{遅|おそ}く{咲|さ}く。
examples.english: Double cherries bloom later than Somei-Yoshino.

examples.japanese: {公園|こうえん}の{八重桜|やえざくら}は{花|はな}びらが{幾重|いくえ}にも{重|かさ}なって{豪華|ごうか}だ。
examples.english: The double cherries in the park have petals layered many times over and look gorgeous.

notes:
A cherry variety with many-petaled ("double") blossoms, contrasted with single-petaled cherries like ソメイヨシノ. Blooms slightly later, in mid- to late spring, and the heavy, ruffled flowers are a popular ornamental sight.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {八重桜|やえざくら}が{咲|さ}く: the double cherries bloom
- {八重桜|やえざくら}の{並木|なみき}: a row of double cherry trees

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ソメイヨシノ: Somei-Yoshino — the common single-petaled cherry that blooms earlier
